implemented_requirements.requirement: Player controls snake with directional inputs (arrow keys / WASD)
implemented_requirements.evidence: on_key() maps keys in DIRS to Snake.turn(); DIRS includes "Up", "Down", "Left", "Right", "w", "a", "s", "d".

implemented_requirements.requirement: Snake moves around the board and updates each tick
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.tick() calls update() then draw(); update() moves the head based on current direction.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Food items appear on empty cells
implemented_requirements.evidence: spawn_food() builds a list of free cells and selects one with random.choice.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Snake grows when it eats food
implemented_requirements.evidence: In update(), if head == self.food, score is increased and the tail is not removed (no pop).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends on collision with self or board boundary
implemented_requirements.evidence: Boundary check: if not (0 <= head[0] < COLS ...) -> state = "over"; self‑collision check: if head in (s.body if eating else s.body[:-1]) -> state = "over".

implemented_requirements.requirement: Current score is displayed on the HUD
implemented_requirements.evidence: draw() creates a text element with f"Score: {self.score}" in the HUD rectangle.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Multiple difficulty levels affect game speed
implemented_requirements.evidence: config.SPEEDS defines "Easy", "Medium", "Hard"; menu selection (keys 1‑3) sets self.difficulty; tick() uses SPEEDS[self.difficulty] for after().

implemented_requirements.requirement: Board is redrawn after each move
implemented_requirements.evidence: draw() clears canvas and redraws grid, food, snake, HUD each tick.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Menu for difficulty selection and game‑over overlay
implemented_requirements.evidence: state "menu" shows overlay with difficulty options; state "over" shows win/lose overlay.

critical_issues: None evident: the code is self‑contained, uses only the standard library (tkinter) and appears logically correct.
judge.summary: The provided files implement a fully functional classic Snake game meeting all core requirements: directional control, food spawning, growth, collision detection, scoring, HUD, and selectable difficulty levels. The code is complete, logically sound, and likely executable on any Python environment with tkinter. No critical defects were found.
